scope: apps/api/src/middlewares/auth.ts, apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts, apps/web portal layouts, schema.prisma Priest model
auditor: main-loop-direct (agent retries died with proxy socket errors — fallback per multi-agent-mandatory-execution doctrine)

findings.title: Priest verification gate is dead: PANDIT role + auto-created active Priest = any self-signup user becomes a verified priest
findings.evidence: requireRole('priest') line 337: `if (userRoles.includes('PANDIT')) return;` — grants access on PANDIT role ALONE, BEFORE the status check at line 356 (`if (!priest || priest.status !== 'active')`). The status check is unreachable for PANDIT holders. getPriestId (priest.ts:75-86) auto-creates a Priest via `prisma.priest.create({ data: { userId, displayName, specializations, languages, experienceYears, bio } })` — it does NOT set status or verificationStatus, so schema defaults apply: `status @default(active)` (schema:305) and `verificationStatus @default(pending)` (schema:301). auth.ts:783-838 SIGNUP_ROLE_ENUM lets a user POST /signup with role:'pandit' → UserRoleAssignment.create({role:'PANDIT'}) with NO approval step.
findings.impact: Any unauthenticated visitor can self-signup as role='pandit' (no approval), then call any /api/v1/priest/* endpoint: requireRole('priest') returns on PANDIT, getPriestId auto-creates an ACTIVE priest record, and they have full priest powers — accepting pujas, marking bookings complete, uploading video proof, (once payouts are wired) receiving payouts. The entire priest-verification/onboarding-approval model is bypassable. Logged-in impact; also degrades trust for logged-out devotees who assume priests are verified.
findings.repro: 1. POST /api/v1/auth/signup {email, password, role:'pandit', fullName} → 200, UserRoleAssignment PANDIT created. 2. POST /api/v1/auth/login → token. 3. GET /api/v1/priest/dashboard → 200 (getPriestId auto-creates active Priest). 4. Accept/complete a booking via PATCH /api/v1/bookings/:id (see C1). Expected: signup-as-pandit requires admin approval; /priest/* requires status=active + verificationStatus=verified. Observed: full access immediately.
findings.suggestedFix: Two-part: (a) requireRole('priest') — REMOVE the early `if (userRoles.includes('PANDIT')) return;`. Always run the priest-lookup + require `priest.status === 'active' && priest.verificationStatus === 'verified'`. Only ADMIN may waive. (b) Signup — do NOT let /signup self-assign any role other than DEVOTEE. A 'pandit' (or any provider) role request must create a Lead/Pending profile (onboarding.service.ts) and require admin approval before UserRoleAssignment is written. (c) getPriestId — do NOT auto-create an active Priest; if no Priest row exists, 403 'priest account not onboarded' (it should only be created by the onboarding/approval flow with status=pending). (d) Re-run priest.service tests + add: signup-as-pandit does NOT yield priest powers until admin approves.

findings.title: No apps/web/middleware.ts — all 6 portal layouts gated client-side only; logged-out/non-role users receive the full portal HTML/JS shell before redirect
findings.evidence: Confirmed no apps/web/middleware.ts. All portal layouts use <AuthGuard allowedRoles=[...]> which runs in a client useEffect — the server renders the portal shell (nav, sidebar, page chrome) to a 200 response, THEN the client checks the session and redirects. API routes remain protected (requireRole server-side), so no data leak, but the shell (nav labels, route structure, sometimes static placeholder text) is visible to anyone hitting /admin etc. directly.
findings.impact: Logged-out or wrong-role users see a brief flash of the portal shell (nav/labels) on /admin, /priest, /store-admin, /astrologer-portal, /wellness-portal, /gaushala-portal before client redirect. No data exfiltration (API gated), but it leaks portal structure and is a poor auth boundary. Low severity; medium if any portal page hardcodes sensitive constants.
findings.repro: 1. Open a fresh browser (no session). 2. Visit https://darshya.online/admin. Expected: server redirects to /auth/login before render. Observed: portal shell HTML renders (200), then client redirects.
findings.suggestedFix: Add apps/web/middleware.ts that checks the session cookie/token and redirects unauthenticated/non-role users from /admin/**, /priest/**, /store-admin/**, /astrologer-portal/**, /wellness-portal/**, /gaushala-portal/** to /auth/login before the page renders. NOTE: memory reference_bhaktisetu_cf_pages_no_middleware says middleware.ts was a build-breaker on the OLD Cloudflare Pages deploy — but prod is now Render Node standalone (reference_darshya_cf_pages_next_on_pages_dead), so middleware is safe to add. Verify the build still passes.

findings.title: Demo-token ADMIN bypass (demo-admin → ADMIN) — guarded by boot-fatal + prod reject, but a prod env misconfigure (ALLOW_DEMO_TOKENS=true) would re-arm it
findings.evidence: DEMO_ROLE_MAP maps 'admin' → ['ADMIN','DEVOTEE'] (auth.ts:122). Defenses: line 98-99 `demoAllowed = NODE_ENV !== 'production' || ALLOW_DEMO_TOKENS === 'true'`; line 104 rejects demo tokens when !demoAllowed; line 11-15 boot-fatal: `if (ALLOW_DEMO_TOKENS==='true' && NODE_ENV==='production') process.exit(1)`. Same gate on /login demo accounts (auth.ts:645). DEPLOY.md:15 sets NODE_ENV=production.
findings.impact: In correctly-configured prod (NODE_ENV=production, ALLOW_DEMO_TOKENS unset): demo-admin token is 401-rejected; cannot become admin. The bypass is only re-armed if an operator sets ALLOW_DEMO_TOKENS=true in prod — but the boot guard crashes the server first, so it cannot serve traffic. Defense-in-depth is strong. Low severity (residual misconfig risk only).
findings.repro: 1. In prod (NODE_ENV=production, no ALLOW_DEMO_TOKENS): curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer demo-admin-...' /api/v1/admin/users → 401 'Demo tokens not accepted in production.' 2. If operator sets ALLOW_DEMO_TOKENS=true in prod → API process exits at boot (FATAL log).
findings.suggestedFix: No code change needed (guards are correct). Defense-in-depth: add a deploy-time check / Render env validation that refuses ALLOW_DEMO_TOKENS=true in the prod service. Optionally add a test asserting the boot-fatal guard. Ensure ALLOW_DEMO_TOKENS is absent (not 'false') in prod env to avoid any string-truth edge.

summary: 3 findings (1 critical, 2 low). The critical (ag-01) is the real find: priest verification is dead because requireRole('priest') short-circuits on PANDIT and getPriestId auto-creates an active Priest — any self-signup-as-pandit user bypasses the whole verified-priest model. The demo-admin bypass (ag-03) is REFUTED-for-prod (boot-fatal guarded) — logged as low defense-in-depth. No-web-middleware (ag-02) confirms prior #31, low. NOTE: a deeper auth.ts signup/session review (token refresh, expiry edge cases, password-hash verify path) was not exhaustively done by the main loop due to proxy-failed agent retries — recommend a focused agent re-run once the proxy stabilizes.
